transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Oh, hello Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Well... I suppose I'm here because my family thought it might be a good idea for me to talk to someone. I've always been a very active person, which is a blessing at seventy, don't you think? But... I do feel like I’m just always up and moving around. Even on what is supposed to be a quiet day at home, I find myself bouncing from sorting the garden club list, over to my knitting bag, and then suddenly I'm pulling out travel papers... usually before I’ve really finished any one of those things. 

I just like to keep busy, you know? But I suppose it can be a bit exhausting sometimes, and my daughter noticed I've been a little scattered. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it alright.
Do you feel like you're moving from one thing to another because you can't seem to settle or sit still?

Well, I wouldn't say I absolutely *can't* sit still, because I certainly can if I need to. I always try to be polite about that in company. But I suppose... well, if I have to sit in one place for too long, I do get this sort of, oh, stirred-up feeling inside? 

It’s not a bad feeling, really, just a little urge like I need to stand up and straighten a picture frame, or maybe go check on something in the kitchen. I always just thought of it as wanting to be helpful and keeping a tidy house. Is that the sort of thing you mean? I hope I'm answering your questions properly.
Do you feel restless when you're not actively doing something?

Yes, exactly... I suppose that's what I was trying to explain just a moment ago. If I'm not actively busy with a project and I have to just sit still for too long, I do get that... well, that stirred-up feeling inside. 

It’s just a little nudge telling me to stand up and straighten something out, or go check on things around the house. I wouldn't want you to think I'm jumping out of my skin or anything terrible like that! It's very mild, really. Just a... a desire to be productive, I suppose. Does that sound like what you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm understanding you properly and giving you the right information.
Do you feel anxious or worried when you have that stirred-up feeling inside?

Oh, no, not anxious. Goodness, no. I wouldn't want you to think I'm a worrywart or anything like that. It's really just a... a physical sort of energy, I suppose? 

I don't feel nervous or upset when it happens. It's more like my body is just reminding me that there are things to be done, like folding the laundry or tending to the hydrangeas. I always try to look on the bright side, and having a bit of extra pep at my age is something to be thankful for, isn't it? I hope that makes sense... I'm not making it sound like I'm terribly stressed, am I?
Are you finding it difficult to complete tasks or projects because you're moving from one thing to another?

Oh, well... no, I wouldn't say I find it difficult, exactly. I mean, I do move around a bit, like I said, just keeping busy with little things around the house. But I always manage to get everything done eventually! 

Sometimes I might start a bit of dusting in the living room and then remember I need to water the plants on the porch, so I'll go do that for a moment. But I always come back to the dusting. It's really just... multitasking, isn't it? I think it's quite normal for a woman my age who takes pride in keeping a nice home. I'm certainly not leaving things in a dreadful mess or anything like that. I hope that's the right sort of answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm disorganized or... or flighty.
Do you feel like your need to keep busy and move from one task to another is interfering with your relationships or daily life?

Oh... well... I wouldn't want to use a harsh word like "interfering." That makes it sound so dreadful, like I'm ruining things! But... well, I suppose if I'm being perfectly honest... it has caused a little bit of a fuss lately. 

Just a... a bit of strain at home with my husband, and over at the community center where I volunteer. It's nothing terrible, really! It's just that... well, they feel like they can't always count on me to keep our plans straight. Because I'm always bustling about from one thing to the next, I might mix up a time or a detail, so my husband and the other volunteers have started sort of... checking behind me. Just to make sure I haven't gotten things muddled up. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, if I'm honest. I really do try my very best to be helpful, and I'd hate for anyone—especially you—to think I'm undependable. I just want to be useful, you know? Do you think it's alright that I get a little mixed up sometimes? I hope I'm answering your question properly...
Do you feel like your need to keep busy is causing you a lot of distress?

Oh, distress? Oh, my, no. Goodness, I wouldn't use a word like that at all! I'm really a very cheerful person, I promise you. 

I don't sit around feeling upset or... or distressed about any of it. I just like to keep my hands busy, you know? I think it's much better to be active than to just sit in a rocking chair all day, don't you agree? I mean, even if I get a little turned around sometimes and cause a bit of a fuss for my husband, it doesn't make me terribly sad or anything. I just count my blessings that I still have the energy to putter about at my age. 

I hope that's a good sign? I really wouldn't want you to worry about my mood, Doctor. I'm quite happy, really I am!
Have you had to cut back on any activities or responsibilities because of your difficulty with sitting still or completing tasks?

Oh, heavens, no. I haven't stopped doing anything. I... well, I would feel just awful if I had to give up my responsibilities. 

I still do all my usual things around the house, and I'm still at the community center every week. I might take a little longer to finish setting up the tables or organizing the donations because I'm... you know, buzzing about from one spot to another, but I always make sure it gets done. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was becoming a burden or shirking my duties just because I can't sit quietly! 

I just keep right on going. I think it's so important to stay involved and carry your own weight, don't you? I hope it's a good sign that I'm still doing all my normal activities. I certainly wouldn't want you to think I was giving up!
Have you noticed any problems at work or in your social relationships because of your difficulty with staying focused on one task?

Oh, well... I know we touched on this just a moment ago, and I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is... but, yes, I suppose it has caused a little bit of a bump in the road socially. 

I wouldn't call it a "problem," exactly! But... well, it has started causing some real strain at home with my husband, and over at the community center. It's just that they feel they can't quite count on me to keep our plans straight anymore without someone checking behind me. Because I get so caught up moving from one little chore to the next, I might lose the thread of what we were supposed to be doing. 

I feel just terrible about it, I really do. I hate being a bother to them when they have to double-check my work or remind me of the schedule. I do try to be so careful! Do you think they'll understand that I don't mean to be difficult? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a terrible nuisance... I just want to be honest with you, like you asked. Is that the sort of thing you needed to know?
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Oh, goodness, no. I... I really don't think I do that. I know I flutter about a bit, like we talked about, but I wouldn't say I just jump into things without thinking. 

I try to be very careful, actually! I always want to make sure I'm doing the right thing, you know, so I don't upset anyone or cause any extra trouble for my husband. I like to think things over before I make any real decisions. I certainly wouldn't want to make a foolish mistake at my age! 

Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm understanding your question right, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Are you having trouble meeting your responsibilities at the community center because of your difficulty with focusing on one task?

Oh, dear... well, I suppose this goes right back to what I was just confessing to you a few minutes ago. I hate to sound like a broken record, and I really do try my hardest to get everything finished! But... yes, I suppose I am having a little trouble with it. 

Like I mentioned, it really has started causing some real strain at the community center, and with my husband at home, too. The other volunteers, they just feel like they can't quite count on me to keep our plans straight anymore. Not unless someone comes along behind me to double-check what I've done. 

I feel just awful having to admit that to you again. It’s so embarrassing to need people checking up on me at my age, like a child. I promise I'm doing my very best to focus, Doctor, I really am. I hope you don't think too poorly of me for struggling with it. I am answering your questions alright, aren't I? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
Are you having trouble maintaining relationships with friends or family due to your difficulty with staying focused on tasks?

Oh, goodness... well, I know we keep circling back to this, and I really hope I'm not misunderstanding what you're looking for! But, yes, it's just like I was mentioning a moment ago. 

I certainly wouldn't say my relationships are falling apart—oh, goodness, no! But... there is definitely that strain at home with my husband, and with my friends over at the community center. Because I get so easily sidetracked, they just feel like they can't count on me to keep our plans straight anymore unless they check behind me. 

I feel just awful that it causes friction with the people I care about, especially when they have to treat me like I need a babysitter. I do try so very hard to stay on top of things so I don't upset them. Is that what you were asking, Doctor? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right answers and not just repeating myself too much!
Have you noticed that your difficulties with staying focused and completing tasks are significantly interfering with your ability to fulfill your roles at home or in the community?

Oh, dear... well, I know we keep coming back to this, and I hope I'm not frustrating you by saying the same things over again. I really do want to give you a good answer. 

But, yes, I suppose it is interfering, like you said. It's just... well, it's just like I mentioned before about the strain it's causing. My husband at home, and the lovely people I volunteer with at the community center... they just feel like they can't quite depend on me to keep all our plans straight anymore. Not without double-checking everything I do, anyway. 

I wouldn't say I'm completely failing at my responsibilities, I really do try my absolute best! But I know it's hard on them, having to always check up on me. I feel terrible about it, I really do. I hope that answers your question properly, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things the way you need me to.
Do you feel like your difficulties with staying focused and completing tasks are causing you significant emotional upset or distress?

Oh, goodness... well, I wouldn't say "distress," exactly. That sounds so... so dramatic, doesn't it? I certainly don't want to make a mountain out of a molehill. 

I mean, yes, I do feel a little embarrassed when people have to check up on me, like I mentioned. It's not a wonderful feeling, knowing I'm causing a bit of friction or letting things slip. But I wouldn't say I'm sitting at home crying about it or anything like that! I mostly just try to keep my chin up and do better tomorrow. 

I hope I'm not making light of what you're asking, Doctor. I just don't want you to think I'm falling to pieces over it. I'm handling it all right, I think... is that the sort of thing you were wondering about?
Do you often find yourself interrupting others or blurting out answers before they finish speaking?

Oh, dear... well, I wouldn't say I'm rude or anything! I really try to be polite, I promise. But... well, I suppose my husband might tell you that I sometimes jump in before he's quite done with his sentence. 

And, oh, I suppose it happens a little bit at the community center, too, during our planning meetings. But it's not because I don't care what they're saying! It's just... if I get an idea, I get so worried that it'll just fly right out of my head if I don't say it that very second. So it just sort of pops out. 

I do try to catch myself, though, and apologize right away. I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly ill-mannered, Doctor? I just get so anxious about forgetting my thought, you see. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often feel like you're acting on impulse without fully thinking through the consequences of your actions?

Oh, my... no, I don't believe so. I certainly hope not! I really try to be quite sensible about things. 

I mean, I know I just mentioned speaking a little out of turn sometimes, but as for actually doing things without thinking... no, I really don't think I do that. I'd absolutely hate to cause any real trouble or, goodness, put anyone in a bad spot by being reckless. I always try to be very careful about my choices and how they might affect my husband or the folks at the center. 

Is that what you were asking, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you often do things without thinking them through?

Oh, goodness, I feel like we might have just touched on this, haven't we? I really don't think I do things without thinking them through. 

I mean, I try to be very considerate and practical. I'd be terribly upset with myself if I just went about doing things willy-nilly and caused a mess for someone else. I really do try to weigh things out, especially if it involves my husband or my friends. 

I hope I'm understanding your question properly? I just want to make sure I'm not repeating myself too much, Doctor. I really do try to be thoughtful about my actions.
Are you finding it harder to manage your daily responsibilities or maintain your relationships due to your difficulties with staying focused and completing tasks?

Oh, dear... I really hate to admit this part. It makes me feel just awful, because I truly try my best to be helpful to everyone. 

But... well, I suppose if I'm being completely honest, it has started causing a bit of a real strain. Mostly at home, and... and over at the community center. It's just so embarrassing to say, but my husband and the other volunteers... well, they can’t really count on me to keep our plans straight lately. Not without someone sort of... checking behind me to make sure I haven't mixed things up or lost track of what I was supposed to be doing. 

I really don't mean to be a burden to them, Doctor, and they are so very patient with me. I just feel terrible when I let them down. Does that... does that answer what you were asking? I hope I don't sound like I'm completely incapable or not trying hard enough.
Do you often engage in impulsive behaviors, such as buying things on impulse or saying things without thinking?

Oh, my... well, I really do feel like we might be going over the same ground a little bit, Doctor. I'm so sorry if I wasn't clear before! 

I really don't think I'm an impulsive person. I certainly try not to be! I mean, I'm on a fixed income, so I definitely don't go around buying things on a whim—my husband and I are very careful with our budget. And as for saying things without thinking... well, like I mentioned earlier, I might occasionally speak out of turn, but I truly don't mean any harm by it. I'd hate for you to think I'm just blurting things out and hurting people's feelings. I always try to be polite and considerate. 

I hope I'm not frustrating you by giving the same sort of answers, Doctor. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I am. Is this what you need to know?
Do you often find yourself doing things without considering how they might affect others?

Oh, dear... I feel a little silly, Doctor, because I really do think this is sort of what we were just talking about. I hope I'm not being difficult or misunderstanding you? 

But no, I truly don't do things without considering other people. Goodness, if anything, I probably worry a bit too much about how everyone else is feeling! My husband and my friends mean the world to me, and I would just be absolutely heartbroken if I ever acted selfishly or did something that caused them any trouble. I always try my very best to put others first and be as considerate as I can be. 

Am I... am I answering these questions the right way for you? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you what you need for your notes.
